<question>
These passages come from two different applications. Summarise what each one claims about frequency-modulated continuous-wave LiDAR and how they differ, citing the passage behind each statement.
</question>
context_chunks:
<chunk id="US12392653B2::claims::p0001">
1. A coherent optical ranging system, comprising a silicon-photonic optical phased array configured to steer a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, and a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection. (Applicant: Robert Bosch GmbH.)
</chunk>

<chunk id="EP3664321A1::claims::p0001">
1. A coherent optical ranging system, comprising a silicon-photonic optical phased array configured to steer a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, and a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection, wherein a chirp non-linearity is corrected using a reference interferometer having a fixed delay. (Applicant: Beamforge Semiconductor Co., Ltd.)
</chunk>

<chunk id="EP3664321A1::desc::p0066">
The approach of the present application differs from earlier proposals in that no additional processing step is required to address the cost and reliability penalty of mechanically scanned time-of-flight LiDAR in automotive service.
</chunk>

args.summary: The two applications claim similar coherent FMCW LiDAR systems built around a silicon-photonic optical phased array and balanced photodetector pair, but the Beamforge Semiconductor application (EP3664321A1) adds a chirp-linearization feature not present in the Bosch application (US12392653B2). A description passage within EP3664321A1 further asserts that its approach avoids an additional processing step needed to offset the cost and reliability drawbacks of mechanically scanned time-of-flight LiDAR, which appears to be in tension with its own claim requiring a correction step via a reference interferometer.

key_points.text: US12392653B2, applied for by Robert Bosch GmbH, claims a coherent optical ranging system with a silicon-photonic optical phased array that steers a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, paired with a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection.

EP3664321A1, applied for by Beamforge Semiconductor Co., Ltd., claims the same core system (silicon-photonic optical phased array steering a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part and a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection) but adds correction of chirp non-linearity using a reference interferometer having a fixed delay.
The key difference between the two claims is that EP3664321A1 includes the chirp non-linearity correction limitation, while US12392653B2 does not include this element.

A description passage in EP3664321A1 states that its approach differs from earlier proposals because it requires no additional processing step to address the cost and reliability penalty of mechanically scanned time-of-flight LiDAR in automotive service, which appears inconsistent with the claim's requirement of a chirp non-linearity correction step.
